clue.text: Obscure English rock band

definitions.meaning: to obscure is to ..., make indistinct
A Britpop group formed in London in 1988

explanation.surface: A little-known English rock group gets a mention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' reads as an adjective (little-known) but works as the verb meaning to smudge.
explanation.definitionFit: Blurring a view hides its detail; the band of that name led the 1990s Britpop scene.

clue.text: Unlawful act beginning to annexe part of Ukraine

parts.note: a crime is an act against the law

indicators.note: the beginning of the word annexe supplies only its opening letter

explanation.surface: An illegal annexation of a region of Ukraine, as happened in 2014.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula on the Black Sea is internationally recognised as Ukrainian territory.

clue.text: Liqueur with rum chaser? True

indicators.note: rum in its old British sense of odd or strange tells us to reshuffle the letters

explanation.surface: A drink of liqueur followed by a rum chaser, apparently confirmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' poses as the spirit but is the adjective meaning strange, which signals the anagram of CHASER and TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a herbal French liqueur made by Carthusian monks.

clue.text: Look over the top of big old summerhouse

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, what follows

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: Looking across the roof of a large old garden summerhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small garden pavilion or summerhouse giving a view.

clue.text: Dessert? Unable to finish second course!

indicators.note: the pudding cannot reach its end, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: syllabub is a frothy pudding of whipped cream and wine

explanation.surface: A diner too full to finish the dessert misses the next course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks like a meal course but means a course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabus is the outline of topics covered by a course of study.

clue.text: Starts to open some letters offering capital

indicators.note: the starts of the four following words give their initial letters

explanation.surface: Opening the post to find capital, money, enclosed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money in the letters; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Popular, one-time whistle-blower

parts.note: something in fashion is said to be in
one-time means former, erstwhile

explanation.surface: A once-popular figure who exposed wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: An informer passes secret information to the authorities, as a whistle-blower does.

clue.text: Watch how things pan out as we detain criminal

indicators.note: a criminal rearrangement is a wrongful one, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Holding a criminal while we see how events unfold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' seems to be the person detained but is an adjective signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To wait and see is to hold back from acting until events develop.

clue.text: Type of wood needed to make large bow?

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a bow is a curve, an arch

explanation.surface: Which timber does an archer need for a big longbow?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow' suggests archery, but here it is a curved shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Larch is a deciduous conifer whose timber is widely used.

clue.text: Former name of Red Sea country having deep chasm in one area

definitions.text: Former name of Red Sea country

parts.note: an abyss is a bottomless gulf
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Red Sea country, once differently named, containing a vast ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a positional instruction but just gives its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia was the old name for Ethiopia, which bordered the Red Sea before Eritrea separated.

clue.text: Deep regret about code creator

parts.note: re means concerning, about
Samuel Morse devised Morse code

explanation.surface: A code-maker feels sorry about something he did.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is guilt-ridden sorrow for a wrong committed.

clue.text: Sentry's appearance, old-fashioned

parts.note: a look is an outward appearance
something no longer in style is out

explanation.surface: A guard whose look is dated.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookout is a person posted to keep watch, like a sentry.

clue.text: New tune by Oscar being broadcast

indicators.note: by means next to, placing the letter beside the rest

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A fresh song by someone called Oscar is on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' sounds like a composer but is the radio code word for O.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme on air is being transmitted live.

clue.text: Rather strange how Humpty Dumpty ended up?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for unconventional or eccentric
in the nursery rhyme Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall and had a great fall, ending up literally away from it

explanation.surface: Odd, how the nursery-rhyme egg finished.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for bizarre behaviour, and literally the egg's position after his tumble.

clue.text: Shoot sergeant-major in Gulf state, one investigating complaints

indicators.note: in says the shoot and the sergeant-major go inside the state's name

parts.note: Oman is a country on the Arabian Gulf
a bud is a young shoot

explanation.surface: Shooting a senior soldier in the Gulf brings an official inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' reads as a verb about gunfire but is the noun for a plant sprout.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is an official appointed to look into public grievances.

clue.text: Male entering town (Deal), awfully shabby

indicators.note: entering says the male goes inside the jumbled letters
done awfully means done badly, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man arrives in the Kentish town of Deal, looking very scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles the town and its name into DOWNATEL, which 'entering' opens up for the male. Deal is a seaside town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Down at heel describes someone looking poor and shabby, like worn-down shoes.

clue.text: Something memorable said on the way out?

definitions.text: Something memorable said on the way out?

parts.words: Something memorable said on the way out?
parts.note: leaving, here dying, someone utters a celebrated remark; the idiom also covers an overconfident claim soon proved wrong

explanation.surface: A notable parting remark.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the remark a person makes just before death, the most literal way out.

clue.text: Forming an architectural feature

definitions.meaning: a decorative strip on a wall or ceiling

explanation.definitionFit: To mould is to shape; a moulding is an ornamental band such as a cornice.

clue.text: Player unhappy about each period of extra time

indicators.note: about puts the shuffled letters around the other piece
an unhappy arrangement is an upset one, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A footballer upset at every spell of added time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappy' scrambles the first word into LPYEAR, which 'about' wraps round the abbreviation. 'extra time' suggests football but means an added day.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap year has an extra day, February 29th, making it a longer span.

clue.text: Servant put up mistletoe, initially with help

parts.note: to house someone is to put them up

indicators.note: initially means the word mistletoe gives just its first letter

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A servant hanging Christmas mistletoe with assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' suggests hanging the decoration; it means accommodate.
explanation.definitionFit: A housemaid is a female domestic servant.

clue.text: Mother's accompanying the Spanish lass

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother, with the possessive s
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A mother chaperoning a Spanish girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A damsel is an old word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Stroll out of hazard, abandoning golf

indicators.note: abandoning says the golf letter is left out

parts.note: to hazard is to risk, gamble
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Walking off a golf course hazard after giving up the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hazard' and 'golf' together suggest a bunker; here hazard means a risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: Bishop and former PM briefly in conflict

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: Clement Attlee was UK Prime Minister 1945-51

explanation.surface: A clergyman and an ex-Prime Minister briefly at odds.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle is a fight between armed forces, a conflict.

clue.text: Broad lout backing spiv

parts.note: broad means wide

indicators.note: backing means the word is turned round

parts.note: a yob is a lout

explanation.surface: A burly thug supporting a black marketeer.
explanation.walkthrough: A spiv is British slang for a flashy petty crook dealing in black-market goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide boy is British slang for a man living by sharp, shady dealing.

clue.text: Sculpture shattered

explanation.definitionFit: A bust is a carved portrait; something bust is broken beyond use.

clue.text: Wise man with two degrees describing Dolly Varden?

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing round, encircling

parts.note: MA is the Master of Arts degree, so two of them give it twice over
a Dolly Varden is a wide-brimmed flowered hat, named after a Dickens character

explanation.surface: A doubly qualified sage portraying a Dickens heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense, to draw a line round. Dolly Varden is a character in Barnaby Rudge.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma is a Hindi title for a revered sage, famously given to Gandhi.

clue.text: Countertenor from Deal (town)

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A countertenor singer from the Kentish seaside town of Deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a male singer with a high falsetto range, the same voice as a countertenor.

clue.text: Left with son before head causes scene

indicators.note: before puts the earlier pieces ahead of the headland

parts.note: and means with, together
a head is a headland, a cape

explanation.surface: A departure with a son, ahead of the boss, makes a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a person in charge; it is a promontory.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a view of scenery, a scene of the countryside.

clue.text: Striking effect of chapter in story recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole is read in reverse
in says the chapter letter goes inside the story

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A memorable dramatic moment from a chapter of a remembered story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C into TALE to make TALCE, which 'recalled' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is a borrowing from French for brilliant success or a showy impression.
